reviews.review:
The story is barebone and the gameplay is generic. Luckily there is a Steam Workshop.

Other than that, I can say that it is like Left 4 Dead series but a bit different.

A fresh take on the co-op shooter genre, this game thrusts you and your friends into a chaotic, retro-futuristic universe where teamwork is essential for survival. With its vibrant, colorful art style and fast-paced gameplay, it feels like a love letter to classic sci-fi B-movies. The procedurally generated levels keep each playthrough exciting, while the diverse range of weapons and enemies ensures that no two sessions are the same. Although it’s still polishing its balance and depth, it’s a promising and fun addition to the cooperative shooter scene.

[h1]Left 4 Dead in Retrofuturism[/h1]


[h3]In General[/h3]
Okay, I have mixed feelings about this game.

I've never heard of the game, even though I'm a big Left4Dead and SciFi fan. Which may well be because the game seems to be flying under the radar in general. Which is a shame in itself! 

The game does a lot wrong and even in the apparent 1.0 version still has some bugs / seems unpolished. 

But: There are also a lot of good things. The soundtrack, the artstyle and the graphics themselves are very good! The environment is well styled and the spaceship (or space station?) looks good. 

[h3]Problems in my opinion[/h3]
And there we are with the problem: Aliens flooding a ship ? A space station ? Unfortunately, the story isn't really explained, even Left4Dead managed that better without video sequences. 

And the QA didn't do a perfect job here either. When holding certain weapons, the character (although all wearing long-sleeved clothes) has a hairy, seemingly male forearm. 

Killed enemies tend to fly around the room or clip through walls.

The achievements often trigger without you fulfilling the necessary requirements (although this is a luxury problem).

The enemies feel even less of an obstacle than the zombies from Left4Dead. It feels like there are 100 weapons and grenade types that are visually very well designed, but don't give any real haptic feedback. None of the weapons feel strong or powerful.

The enviroment looks great but is as empty as the deep dark space itself. The style is close to Alien Isolation, it shows the 70s SciFi Art pretty good, mixed with popculture.

[h3]Cat charms ![/h3]
That all sounds very negative now, BUT: I love what the game does right! I love the style and would have loved to work on a game like this. It seems like devs are still working on it, which may be possible as they answer to community posts, which is great, but i think there won´t come much more content, which is sad.

However, in my opinion, the game would have been better off as a story-driven single-player shooter and would have gotten more attention. But that's just my opinion. I would love to see more of this world !

[h3]Result[/h3]
Try the game for yourself, you can't go far wrong for less than 10 euros. And if you're looking for someone to co-op with: Get in touch!
